_comment: THE WISH IS TWENTY-FIVE CARDS DOWN, AND THAT USED TO BE THE SAME AS NOT HAVING ONE.
This is the user's own `references/EldraziDisplacerFlicker/claude_s6_gi5` (saved 2026-09-11,
won T4, 71 decisions) at main ordinal 8 -- the FIRST frame of that game at which the mana
engine is on the battlefield. Eldrazi Displacer under Training Grounds (blink = {C}), two
Peregrine Drakes and a Cloud of Faeries as payloads, three lands worth six on an untap:
Kitchen+Overgrowth 3, Brushland+Fertile Ground 2, Adarkar Wastes 1. RecogniseFlickerLoop:
`ok=1 net=5 refund=6 cost=1`, and it says that on every frame from ordinal 8 to the end.
The hand is EMPTY and the Living Wish is at library index 24. Before
MTG_EDF_GOFF_LIB_DEPTH, ScanHandSinks' library route scanned only the top TWENTY, found no
sink, FlickerGoOffCount returned 0, no plan carried a multi-activation blink -- and
EnumerateMainPlans' `best_any >= 0` short-circuit means ComboOffPossible was then NEVER
CALLED. For fifty-two consecutive decisions of the user's game neither the rule table nor the
trial apply was asked the question at all. The button appeared at ordinal 60, when five Clue
cracks had pulled the wish to index 19 and it slid under the cap -- nothing about the board's
ability to win had changed.
USER, 2026-09-11: 'The key here is that the sooner the Combo Off line kicks in the better.
The reason is that the search should have an easy way to query it and be able to skip a huge
chain of operations.' And, bounding it: 'I think it's fair that some of the pieces (those to
generate mana at least) should be on board first.' They are, here, and on this board that is
all the user's rule asks for.
THE LEVER IS THIS FIXTURE'S NEGATIVE CONTROL:
CO_ENV='MTG_EDF_GOFF_LIB_DEPTH=0' bash test/combo_off_check.sh   -> this fixture ABSENT
and edf_co_23 is the control in the other direction -- the same board with every Living Wish
gone from the library, which must stay absent with the lever ON.
Reconstruction caveat, inherited from test/combo_off_frames.py: floating mana cannot be
staged, so this asks the frame with an EMPTY pool. The user's real ordinal-8 frame held
{C:1}; every later frame of that turn held far more. So this is a strictly HARDER board than
the one the button really has to answer for -- and `opponent_life` is 16 rather than 20 for
exactly that reason, stated rather than quietly chosen: at 20 this board is still OFFERED
(rule WISH-DRAW) and the apply lands SIXTEEN of the twenty drains it needs, because the pool
the real frame carried is the part a --scenario fixture cannot stage. The real frame IS
verified, and the one-line proof is the replay itself:
python3 test/combo_off_replay_hunt.py --first-fire --ref-filter claude_s6_gi5 \
--skip autonomous
which reports engine-on-board at frame 14 (ordinal 8), rule fire at frame 14, first VERIFIED
fire at frame 19 (ordinal 13) -- against ordinal 60 with the lever off.
